title: [model] add GLM-5.3-Flash training support
bodyExcerpt:
# What does this PR do? Adds GLM-5.3-Flash support to the v0 training pipeline with the `glm5_next` template. - Adds the chat template with preserved thinking, response EOS handling, and tool-call formatting. - Adds image and video preprocessing through the native Transformers processors, including video timestamps and multimodal token type IDs. - Registers the language model, vision backbone, and multimodal projector modules for freezing and LoRA target selection. Use `template: glm5_next` in the training configuration. ## Validation Ran full SFT with FSDP2 and DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 using the original BF16 checkpoint with the text model reduced to its first 4 layers. All 24 vision layers were retained, with the vision backbone and multimodal projector frozen. The reduced text model includes both KDA and sparse attention, as well as dense and MoE layers. - Dataset: `data/mllm_demo.json`. - Setup: 16 devices, batch size 2 per device, gradient accumulation 1, sequence length 2048, BF16, learning rate `1e-5`, 50 steps. - Environment: PyTorch `2.10.0`, Transformers `5.17.0.dev0`, Accelerate `1.11.0`, DeepSpeed `0.18.4`. | Backend | First-step loss | Step-15 loss | | --- | ---: | ---: | | FSDP2 | 11.453125 | 0.04920959 | | DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 | 11.461189 | 0.04505016 | ## Training configurations
Reference YAML files 1. Set `text_config.num_hidden_layers` to 4. 2. Truncate `layer_types`, `mlp_layer_types`, and `indexer_types` to their first 4 entries. 3. Retain all 24 vision layers. ### FSDP2 training configuration: ```yaml model_name_or_path: /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash low_cpu_mem_usage: false trust_remote_code: true flash_attn: disabled do_train: true finetuning_type: full freeze_vision_tower: true freeze_multi_modal_projector: true template: glm5_next d

title: [data] fix GLM-4V video prompt expansion for multiple videos
bodyExcerpt:
# What does this PR do?

Fixes #9447

`GLM4VPlugin.process_messages` expanded every `<video>` placeholder with the frame
count and the timestamps of the **first** video:

```python
num_frames = video_grid_thw[0][0] if len(video_grid_thw) > 0 else 0  # hard code for now
```

A sample with two videos of different lengths therefore got the first video's frame
count twice, while the visual tower still produced one entry per frame of *each*
video, so the prompt and the features disagree. `Qwen3VLPlugin` had the same line and
lost it in #10518; `GLM4VPlugin` kept it.

Measured on `zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking` with a 4-frame and an 8-frame video
(`video_grid_thw = [[2, 4, 4], [4, 4, 4]]`, so 2 + 4 = 6 frames are expected):

| | `<|begin_of_image|>` blocks | timestamps |
|---|---|---|
| before, transformers 4.55.0 | 4 | `0 1` / `0 1` |
| after | **6** | `0 1` / `0 1 2 3` |

The frame token budget now matches `sum(grid.prod() // merge_size ** 2)`, which is
what the model is going to hand back.

## The metadata contract

The same method could not run at all on transformers >= 4.57: the metadata still used
the pre-4.57 `VideoMetadata` field name and passed `images=None` to the video
processor.

```
TypeError: VideoMetadata.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'total_frames'
```

That part is the same change as #10538 (open since June, still against an older base),
and it is included here because the multi-video fix is not reachable without it. One
thing #10538 does not cover: transformers >= 4.57 also dropped the `timestamps` key
that carried the frame timestamps, and answers with `video_metadata` instead. With
only the metadata change applied, on transformers 4.57.1 the crash is gone but every
frame is stamped `0`:

```
...<|end_of_image|>0<|begin_of_image|>...<|end_of_image|>0<|end_of_video|>
```

So `_get_frame_timestamps` reads whichever of the two the installed version answers
with (`metadata.timestamps[::2]` for mrope, matching `Glm4vProcessor`), and
